title: fix(types): refuse `operators` on `object-grid` by name, naming the upstream spelling
body:
Fixes #9739

Maintainer ruling 2026-09-18, **letter C**: `operators` leaves the published mirror, a tombstone takes its place that refuses the key by name and names the spelling the upstream protocol declares, and the TypeScript twin does not gain the key.

**Clause-②: no** — evidence below, measured rather than inherited.

---

## The order pointed at the wrong file — read this first

The dispatch fenced this work to `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts`, quoting the line `operators: z.array(FilterOperatorSchema).optional().describe('Available operators')`. That line is real, and it is **a different key**. It was not touched.

The key the ruling governs lives in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`, on `ObjectGridSchema`. Six independent readings agree, and they agree against the file the order named:

| Reading | `complex.zod.ts` `FilterFieldSchema.operators` | `objectql.zod.ts` `ObjectGridSchema.operators` |
|---|---|---|
| Card title: "read by nothing" | **read** — `filter-builder.tsx` reads it for the operator bucket | no reader (byte ruler, objectui#9729) |
| Card title: "absorbed as `any` by the twin" | twin declares it **concretely** as `FilterBuilderOperator[]` | twin is silent; `BaseSchema`'s index signature absorbs it |
| Card: the source comment reads "missed last scan but common" | no such comment | trailing comment says exactly that, verbatim |
| Card's own dedupe words | — | name `ObjectGridSchema` |
| Ruling's words: "the grid component" | filter-builder | object-grid |
| The instrument card objectui#9729 left behind | — | `mirror-only-published-keys-9729.test.ts` names this pair |

Editing the file the order named would have deleted a live, parity-holding key that a renderer reads — the opposite of the ruling. Per the dispatch's own instruction that its file/line pointer is a reading and must be re-derived, it was re-derived, and the correction is declared here rather than made quietly.

## The upstream spelling is measured, not remembered

The ruling's message template carries a placeholder for the upstream spelling (spelled as a word here, never in angle brackets, because GitHub eats tag-shaped fragments). The answer is **`operations`**, and it is the protocol's own word for the rename, not an inference:

```
$ node -e "parse two documents through @objectstack/spec 17.4.0 ObjectGridPropsSchema"

TARGET  { operators: {...} }  => success: false
    unrecognized_keys ["operators"] | Unrecognized key(s) on this `object-grid`:
    `operators`. Did you mean `operators` -> `operations`? ...
CONTROL { operations: {...} } => success: true
CONTROL-LIT { zzNoSuchKey: 1 } => success: false
    unrecognized_keys ["zzNoSuchKey"] | Unrecognized key(s) on this `object-grid`:
    `zzNoSuchKey`. ...    (no rename clause)
CONTROL-BARE {} baseline     => success: true
```

The lit control is what makes the rename a protocol statement rather than boilerplate: an arbitrary unknown key is refused by the same strict object and gets **no** "Did you mean" clause. The version is the one `packages/types` pins (`^17.4.0`, installed `17.4.0`). The test suite re-derives both halves against that installed pin, so a future upstream rename reddens a pin instead of leaving a stale instruction inside an error message.

## What landed

- **`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`** — the member becomes a `retirementTombstone()`, the shape this same directory already carries (`viewTabBar` on the object-view node, `aria` on `DashboardConfigSchema`). Message: `` `operators` is not a key of this component; you meant `operations`. `` The key stays **declared**, which is the whole mechanism: on a `.passthrough()` base an undeclared key is kept unexamined, so only a member can refuse.
- **`object-grid-operators-tombstone-9739.test.ts`** (new) — the bidirectional pin the ruling's execution note calls for: the refused key red, the correct key beside it still green, plus the upstream re-derivation and the twin's deliberate silence.
- **`mirror-only-published-keys-9729.test.ts`** — the pin that asserted the old **acceptance** now asserts the **refusal**. It was not relaxed to pass: its lit control is retained and is doing strictly more work than before, since it now separates "this key is refused" from "this object turned strict".
- **`zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`** — the `MirroredUndeclared` docblock. The row **stays**, and the docblock now says why: that ledger measures *the mirror states a key the twin does not*, and a tombstone is still a stated member. The `aria` row above it has been a tombstone all along, which is the precedent.
- **changeset** — `@object-ui/types` minor, carrying the BREAKING-for-the-misspelling note.

The TypeScript twin is untouched by design. Declaring the key there was the option the ruling refused.

## Clause-②: no — the measurement

Three instruments over the non-test diff, which is exactly one file. Every zero carries a lit control on the same instrument and corpus.

| Instrument | Reading | Lit control on the same instrument |
|---|---|---|
| Exported symbols, comments stripped, `git show origin/main:PATH` vs `HEAD` | 25 -> 25; **0 added**, 0 removed | one synthetic export injected -> instrument reports it |
| Key-set delta across all 23 schemas in that file | **0 keys added**, 0 removed; `ObjectGridSchema` 30 members -> 30 | one synthetic key injected -> instrument reports it |
| Accept set of the one member that moved, both declarations evaluated in one process | key omitted: unchanged · an authored record: **narrowed** · wrong-typed scalar: unchanged · **WIDENED: 0** | a member this diff does not touch discriminates green/red on the same probe |

Comments were stripped before counting by symbol — unstripped, the scan-artefact phrase reads 1, because the comment documenting its removal quotes it; stripped, it reads 0.

The direction is a narrowing toward the protocol: a document that parsed green now parses red, and nothing that parsed red now parses green. The published TypeScript accept set does not move at all — `objectql.ts` is not in the diff.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed — out of scope for this PR and for the three filing classes:

- `ObjectGrid.operatorsInert-9729.test.tsx` in `@object-ui/plugin-grid` still authors `operators` on an `object-grid` node. It is left alone on purpose: it renders and never parses, so it stays green, and what it measures (the renderer draws identical bytes with and without the key) is still true and is now the record of *why* the key was tombstoned. Successor: whoever next touches that file.
- The dispatch asked for a `--pair` exit code against the `needs:contract-review` label. No script in this repo implements that flag (`check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` is the only script that reads the label). Recorded as not measured, with the reason, rather than as an absence.

Per the dispatch, this PR is left in **draft**, unlabelled and un-enqueued; `needs:contract-review` belongs to the seat and was neither added nor removed. The card objectui#9729 that produced the instrument is referenced only — it is not addressed here and remains open.
